aurora.intro: A learning space that brings the essentials together.
aurora.problem: Quizzes, study notes, flashcards, and class participation are closely related parts of learning. Aurora brings them into a shared application, with different workflows for students, lecturers, and administrators.
aurora.roleDescription: I built the frontend and backend, connecting React and TypeScript views to Node and Express REST APIs. I designed MongoDB data models, managed application state and data flow, and deployed the frontend on Vercel.
features: Role-based workspaces
Separate experiences organize the tasks of students, lecturers, and administrators.
Quizzes and room participation
Lecturers can create quizzes, while students join quiz rooms and complete attempts.
Study resources
Notes and flashcard decks support learning beyond a single quiz session.
Performance views
Dashboard views bring learning activity and results into the application.
aurora.architecture: A React and TypeScript frontend manages the interface and client state. It connects to a Node.js and Express REST API, with MongoDB providing document storage. Frontend and backend are maintained in separate public repositories.
aurora.focus: Role-based interfaces, frontend/backend integration, and organizing a complete learning workflow.

floodsentinel.intro: Exploring flood scenarios through maps and machine learning.
floodsentinel.problem: Environmental measurements become easier to explore when their location and context are visible. FloodSentinel is an academic investigation into connecting district-level maps, weather inputs, and a machine-learning pipeline in one interface.
floodsentinel.roleDescription: This is a team project. The repository credits my contribution to the frontend geospatial map and the full machine-learning lifecycle. The wider project also includes weather ingestion and scenario exploration.
features: District-level exploration
A geospatial interface organizes the system around Sri Lankan districts.
Weather inputs
Weather ingestion supplies contextual data for the dashboard and scenario workflow.
Scenario modelling
A Python machine-learning pipeline works with synthetic flood scenarios.
Connected dashboard
A React interface connects map exploration with backend model outputs.
floodsentinel.architecture: React and TypeScript support the dashboard, with Leaflet providing map interactions. A FastAPI backend connects the interface to Python modelling components built with scikit-learn.
floodsentinel.focus: Geospatial interface development and connecting a machine-learning workflow to an application. Synthetic training scenarios are not evidence of real-world prediction accuracy.

resq.intro: A shared command portal for response coordination.
resq.problem: Incident information, team allocation, and evidence can sit in separate workflows. RESQ explores how a command portal and domain services can bring these responsibilities together in a disaster-response application.
resq.roleDescription: This academic project connects a React command portal with dedicated incident, response, and evidence services. Its infrastructure definitions extend the work beyond individual services into the configuration of a cloud-based application.
features: Incident mapping
The portal provides an interface for viewing and working with incident information.
Response coordination
Response workflows organize team allocation and related operational records.
Evidence management
A dedicated domain service supports the management of digital evidence.
Cloud infrastructure
Terraform definitions describe infrastructure alongside the application services.
resq.architecture: A React and TypeScript portal connects to Spring-based domain services. The system separates incident, response, and evidence responsibilities, using service discovery and an API gateway. Infrastructure definitions target Google Cloud.
resq.focus: Separating domain responsibilities and connecting a frontend, services, and cloud infrastructure.

aurora-mobile.intro: A study companion that goes where you go.
aurora-mobile.problem: Study materials should be easy to revisit away from a desktop. Aurora Mobile adapts note organization and flashcard review into a focused mobile experience for managing learning resources on the go.
aurora-mobile.roleDescription: I built the React Native interface, implemented application state with Redux Toolkit, and integrated Firebase authentication and Firestore. I used TypeScript and custom hooks to organize the code, and Expo Application Services to manage the mobile build workflow.
features: Organized notes
Create, retrieve, update, and delete notes from a mobile interface.
Flashcard study
Flashcard decks and study sessions provide a dedicated space for review.
Account access
Email and password authentication is integrated through Firebase Auth.
Personal viewing preferences
Light and dark themes support different reading preferences.
aurora-mobile.architecture: React Native and Expo provide the application foundation. TypeScript and Redux Toolkit organize application data and state, NativeWind supports interface styling, and Firebase supplies authentication and Cloud Firestore persistence.
aurora-mobile.focus: Mobile interaction design, state management, authentication, and cloud-backed study resources.

guestfind.intro: Helping lost belongings find their way back.
guestfind.problem: A lost item creates a sequence of tasks: reporting it, identifying a match, checking a claim, and arranging its return. GuestFind organizes that sequence for hotel staff and guests in a shared web application.
guestfind.roleDescription: This project brings together a Spring Boot REST backend and an HTML, CSS, and JavaScript frontend. Separate administrator, staff, and guest workflows support the different responsibilities in the lost-and-found process.
features: Item reports
Record lost and found belongings so they can be managed through a structured workflow.
Matching and claims
Connect possible matches with a claim review and approval process.
Delivery management
Track the next step after a claim has been approved.
Role-specific access
Different responsibilities are organized for administrators, staff, and guests.
guestfind.architecture: A Java and Spring Boot backend exposes REST APIs and uses Spring Security for access-related functionality. MySQL stores application data, while a browser frontend presents reporting and management workflows.
guestfind.focus: Modelling a multi-step business process and connecting roles, application state, and persistent records.

greenhouse.intro: Connecting the moving parts of greenhouse management.
greenhouse.problem: Zones, sensor readings, automation decisions, and crop records represent different parts of greenhouse operations. This project explores how to model those responsibilities as cooperating services instead of one tightly coupled application.
greenhouse.roleDescription: The public project implements a distributed management system with four domain services. A registry, central configuration server, and gateway provide the supporting service infrastructure.
features: Zone management
Organize greenhouse zones as a distinct application responsibility.
Sensor data
A telemetry service handles sensor-related records and inputs.
Automation rules
Automation actions are separated from the collection of telemetry.
Crop lifecycle
Crop records are managed by their own domain service.
greenhouse.architecture: Java and Spring Cloud provide the service foundation. Eureka supports discovery, a central configuration server coordinates configuration, and an API gateway provides an entry point to the domain services. MySQL supports persistence.
greenhouse.focus: Service boundaries, discovery, central configuration, and coordination across a distributed application.

iso8583.intro: Making payment-message structure easier to explore.
iso8583.problem: Payment protocols are easier to understand when messages can be inspected and request-response exchanges can be reproduced. These Android experiments explore ISO 8583 message parsing and a local POS-to-switch simulation.
iso8583.roleDescription: Two public repositories cover complementary experiments: an Android parser and a simulator. The parser exposes message structure, while the simulator constructs a sale request and exchanges it with a local switch server.
features: Message inspection
Inspect a message header, message type indicator, and individual data elements.
jPOS integration
Use jPOS in the parsing workflow to work with ISO 8583 messages.
POS simulation
Construct a sale request for a controlled development exchange.
Local switch exchange
Use TCP sockets to send a request and receive a response from a local server.
iso8583.architecture: Java-based Android code handles the application and protocol experiment. The parser uses jPOS, while the simulation separates a POS terminal flow from a local switch server communicating over TCP.
iso8583.focus: Protocol structure, message parsing, and socket-based request-response communication in a development environment.

serenity.intro: Organizing the administrative side of care.
serenity.problem: A care center needs to connect people, appointments, programs, and payment records. Serenity is a desktop coursework application focused on organizing these administrative workflows in one system.
serenity.roleDescription: The public JavaFX application includes controllers for patient registration, therapist and program management, therapy sessions, payments, users, and role-specific dashboards. Its Maven configuration includes Hibernate, MySQL, and JasperReports.
features: Patient registration
Manage patient information through a dedicated administration workflow.
Therapists and programs
Keep therapist and program records within the application.
Therapy sessions
Organize session-related records alongside the people and programs involved.
Payments and dashboards
Maintain payment records and present role-specific dashboard interfaces.
serenity.architecture: JavaFX provides the desktop interface and controllers. Hibernate connects domain entities to MySQL persistence, with JasperReports included for reporting functionality.
serenity.focus: Desktop application structure, object-relational mapping, and administrative workflows. This is an academic administration project, not a clinical decision system.
